published_prior_art.cite: Hsieh2026 fixed-weight stacked-DDD inference; ChenSantAnnaXie2025 supplies the close DiD analogue of covariance-optimal efficient aggregation.
OrtizVillavicencioSantAnna2025 optimizes each ATT block; the proposed aggregate-level projection frontier is DDD-specific but rests on standard constrained-GMM geometry.
No inspected DDD paper gives a reuse-graph classification for uniform equality of componentwise and joint aggregate GMM.

soundness_flags.label: Target estimand and def:ddd-law-class
soundness_flags.one_line: P is declared an observed-data law on O but theta and several class restrictions use E_P of potential outcomes, which P does not contain; introduce a full-data law Q with observed marginal P and state the identified observable functional separately.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: thm:joint-system-limit / technical_internal_limitation
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The claimed optimum is only over constant linear loadings of the retained pairwise score vector, not over all regular estimators in the DDD model.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Minimum asymptotic variance within the retained constant-score span under the stated fixed-T, fixed-M regime.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: All closed results / honest_scope
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The claims condition on fixed horizon, fixed target and comparison sets, fixed aggregation weights, nonsingular score covariance, and the stated nuisance-learning regime.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The estimator, limit law, and frontier hold only on the fixed-dimensional staggered-DDD law class M.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper identifies pairwise staggered-DDD ATT scores, combines admissible comparison cohorts by a within-(g,t) inverse-covariance GMM weight, and derives event-study aggregation from those componentwise estimates.
The source gives a fixed-weight stacked event-study CLT and original-unit clustered variance aggregation that accounts for comparison units reused across stacks.

The paper derives closed-form semiparametric efficient DiD and event-study influence functions and covariance-dependent aggregation across comparison groups and baseline periods in fixed-T staggered DiD.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Main text, efficient-influence-function and cross-fitted-estimation theorems
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper develops semiparametric, doubly robust DDD estimators for panel and repeated-cross-section designs and studies their efficiency conditions.
The journal article presents o(N^-1/4) as a crude sufficient common L2 nuisance-rate condition for smooth orthogonal scores, while allowing more refined product-rate requirements in specific models.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Repair the full-data/observed-data distinction: define a full-data law Q, let P=Q_O, state the causal restrictions under Q, and display the identified theta(P) functional used by the scores.

Elevate the DDD-specific contribution beyond constrained-GMM algebra by proving a nontrivial reuse-graph classification theorem with explicit graph conditions and nondegenerate compatible-law witnesses on both sides.

Benchmark the joint estimator against the semiparametric DDD efficiency bound, or prove a precise condition under which the retained-score span attains that bound; this would distinguish the work more sharply from Chen–Sant'Anna–Xie's DiD efficiency construction.

recommended_next_step: Revise the causal-law notation first, then retain the field-tier aggregate-GMM frontier while developing the reuse-graph result or a DDD efficiency-bound comparison as the route to stronger novelty.
